plans.note: Section 9 is the dedicated liability clause; check for mutuality, cap amount tied to fees, exclusion of consequential damages and carve-outs (IP indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence). Section 8's disclaimer may compound the limitation.

Section 8 (INDEMNIFICATION) should carry Commerce One's third-party IP infringement indemnity in our favour; confirm defence/control, no cap-by-reference in Section 9, and that any reciprocal indemnity from us stays narrow.

Grant of Rights plus the defined terms CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY are the likely vehicles for field-of-use or market restrictions on us; also scan Exhibit D sales/marketing cooperation for restraints on competing products.

Check Section 2 (Grant of Rights) and Exhibit D for any obligation to host or resell only Commerce One software, or exclusive ASP/market-segment commitments; preserve our freedom to source competing applications.

Pricing/Payment Terms and the revenue-sharing fee schedule are where a best-pricing or most-favoured-customer clause would sit; an MFN running to Commerce One (e.g. best terms on our hosted offerings) should be resisted, one in our favour retained.

No standalone non-solicit heading; if present it would appear in Miscellaneous or alongside Shared Resources (secondment of personnel). Confirm, and if found require narrow scope, 12 months and a general-advertising carve-out.

Section 11 (Term and Termination) — check whether we have termination for convenience on notice without penalty and whether Commerce One has any unilateral mid-term exit or termination-for-convenience right to remove.
Look in Section 11 for auto-renewal terms and the non-renewal notice window; cross-check Exhibit B pricing for renewal uplift caps.
Governing law/venue and any dispute-resolution or arbitration provision will be in Miscellaneous; California is acceptable given both parties, but confirm courts rather than foreign arbitration.
Assignment clause sits in Miscellaneous; ensure we may assign to affiliates and successors and that our change of control is not a Commerce One termination trigger under Section 11.

Grant of Rights and the DEVELOPMENTS definition drive ownership; verify we retain our own IP, customer data on Corio Servers, and any developments/configurations we fund, with no assignment to Commerce One. Trademark and confidentiality sections may also touch data rights.

Review scope in Section 2 against the SOFTWARE/DEMONSTRATION SOFTWARE, SOFTWARE USER, CUSTOMER(S) and TERRITORY definitions and Exhibit A; the licence must extend to our affiliates, contractors and hosted end customers and must not be revocable at will.

Usage/records audit rights typically ride with the fee and revenue-sharing reporting obligations; require notice, annual frequency, business hours, and Commerce One's cost absent material underpayment.

Check Fees/Payment Terms for late-payment interest, penalties or accelerated fees on termination that function as liquidated damages against us; service credits flowing to us (Exhibit C) are acceptable.

Section 7 (Warranties and Disclaimer) plus the Warranty Period and Acceptance Test definitions; confirm a meaningful duration, a repair/replace/refund remedy, and that the disclaimer does not gut the media/performance warranty. Support levels in Exhibit C are the practical backstop.
No insurance heading in the outline; Commerce One personnel may access Corio Servers under Shared Resources, so propose a standard insurance covenant in Miscellaneous.
Exhibit B pricing, revenue-sharing fees and the IMPLEMENTATION FEE are the likely home for minimum guarantees or take-or-pay volumes; if present, seek an exit or shortfall-only remedy.

Section 11 effects-of-termination and the Section 12 source code escrow are the closest hooks; confirm continued service for our hosted customers, return/deletion of our data and reasonable migration assistance, and add if absent.
